# Python API reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_api_reference.py from the docstrings; do not edit by hand. -->

`import dexvantage as dv` gives every name below without importing Qt. The worked examples are in the [user guide](../user-guide.md#python-api) and [guide/api.md](../guide/api.md); this page is the docstrings of `dexvantage/api.py`, `dexvantage/api_research.py`, `dexvantage/api_cluster.py` and `dexvantage/plugin_sdk.py`, in the order `dv` lists them.

## The module

The Python and notebook API: DexVantage without the window (no Qt is imported on this path).

    import dexvantage as dv

    rig = dv.sample('ur5e')                          # or dv.open('cell.dexv'), dv.new('My cell')
    res = rig.run('coverage')                        # a Result: a dict (the study's JSON) plus .headline, .to_frame()
    res.headline['text']                             # 'Task volume seen: 91.9 % (mostly single or blind)'
    rig.metrics(['coverage.covered', 'bandwidth.payload_mbps'])
    rig.factors['sensor:Overhead D435.z']            # read a factor (core/factors.py paths)
    taller = rig.with_factors({'sensor:Overhead D435.z': 1.2})   # a NEW Rig; rig is unchanged
    rig.factors['sensor:Overhead D435.z'] = 1.2      # edits rig itself (its project is replaced by the edited one)
    rig.export('out/', ['opencv_yaml', 'mjcf'])      # core/exporters: files, notes, a manifest with SHA-256
    rig.check('requirements.yaml')                   # the readiness scorecard (core/requirements.py)
    rig.save('cell.dexv')
    dv.studies(), dv.metrics(), dv.exporters(), dv.plugins()
    ds = dv.datasets.open('path/to/lerobot_dataset')  # LeRobot v2.1 / v3.0, RLDS, ROS 2 bags, plugin formats
    dv.diff(rig, taller), dv.merge(base, ours, theirs)   # project diff and three-way merge (api_research.py)
    dv.bibtex(rig), dv.figure(res, 'fig.svg')        # BibTeX of every source; a vector figure of a result

What edits in place and what returns a new object:

- ``rig.factors[path] = value`` and ``rig.factors.update({...})`` change ``rig`` (its project is replaced by the
  edited copy core.factors.apply returns; Robot and Sensor objects read from it before are then stale).
- ``rig.with_factors({...})``, ``rig.use_variant(name)`` and ``rig.copy()`` return a new Rig; ``rig`` is unchanged.
- ``rig.run(study, **settings)`` runs on a copy with the settings laid over the stored ones; the rig's stored
  settings are unchanged (store them with ``rig.factors['setting:<study>.<key>'] = value``).
- ``rig.robots``, ``rig.sensors`` and ``rig.variants`` are the project's own objects: changing one changes the rig.
- ``rig.add_variant(name, {sensor factors})`` adds a copy of the active variant to ``rig`` (the active one stays).

Every number comes from the studies themselves (the same code the window and batch mode run, through core.jobs and its
result cache, keyed by the project's content): the API computes nothing of its own. A study that cannot run raises
DexVantageError (core.jobs.StudyError) with a plain sentence; a figure a result does not state reads None.

Rig and Result have rich HTML views for Jupyter (_repr_html_). Result.to_frame() returns a pandas DataFrame when
pandas is installed (the optional extra "research": pip install "dexvantage[research]"), else a list of dicts (Records)
whose .note says so.

Doctest (run by tests/test_api.py):

```pycon
>>> import dexvantage as dv
>>> rig = dv.sample('so100')
>>> rig
<Rig 'SO-100 sample': 1 robot, 2 sensors, 1 variant>
>>> [s.name for s in rig.sensors]
['Wrist camera (sample placement)', 'Third-person camera (sample placement)']
>>> z = 'sensor:Third-person camera (sample placement).z'
>>> rig.factors[z]
0.36
>>> higher = rig.with_factors({z: 0.5})               # a new Rig
>>> higher.factors[z], rig.factors[z]
(0.5, 0.36)
>>> rig.factors[z] = 0.4                               # edits rig itself
>>> rig.factors[z]
0.4
>>> res = rig.run('bandwidth')
>>> isinstance(res, dict), res['study'], res.headline['word']
(True, 'bandwidth', 'no hosts')
>>> res.headline['text']
'Smallest controller margin: not stated (no hosts). The rig has no host controller: ...'
>>> 'coverage' in [s['id'] for s in dv.studies()]
True
```

Known limits: the API is a thin layer over the studies, so their own Known limits apply; studies run in the calling
thread (the window's background controller is not used: a long study blocks the notebook cell, pass progress= to see
it move); the result cache is per process (32 results, keyed by content, so a changed project or setting misses it);
UI pages a plugin adds are not reachable from here; HTML views show at most 200 rows of a table.

## Functions

### `dv.open(path: str) -> Rig`

Open a .dexv project as a Rig.

### `dv.sample(name: str) -> Rig`

A sample project as a Rig ('so100', 'ur5e', 'dexhand', 'aloha', 'panda-bimanual', 'g1'; dv.samples() lists
them).

### `dv.new(name: str = 'Untitled') -> Rig`

An empty project as a Rig.

### `dv.samples() -> Table`

No docstring.

### `dv.studies() -> Table`

Every study: id, title, batch flag, whether it needs a robot, and the plugin that added it (None: built in).

### `dv.metrics() -> Table`

Every metric: id, title, unit, better, study, note and the plugin that added it.

### `dv.exporters() -> Table`

No docstring.

### `dv.plugins() -> Table`

The plugins found at start-up (or on first use of the API): name, version, status, what they added, errors.

### `dv.load_plugins(enabled: bool = True, reload: bool = True) -> Table`

Find and load the installed plugins again (enabled=False: list them without loading).

### `dv.runs(where: Rig | str | os.PathLike | RunStore | None = None, *, study: str | list | None = None, tag: str | list | None = None, kind: str | list | None = None, since: str | datetime.date | None = None, until: str | datetime.date | None = None, status: str | list | None = None, project: str | list | None = None) -> Records | pd.DataFrame`

The runs of a run store (run_store(where)) as a table: one row per run (run id, start and end in UTC,
seconds, kind, study, status, project, its content hash, variant, headline, tags, note, re-run of, DexVantage
version, git commit, result hash) and one column per metric (a metric id, or id@stat for a distribution's or a
search's figure); None where a run does not state it. A pandas DataFrame (units in .attrs['units']) when pandas
is installed, else Records (a list of row dicts, with .units). Filters: study, tag, kind, status, project (a
value or a list), since / until (a date, a datetime or ISO text).

### `dv.track(result: Result | dict, rig: Rig | None = None, *, store: str | os.PathLike | RunStore | None = None, tags: tuple | list = (), note: str = '') -> dict`

Log a Result (from rig.run or rig.check) as a run, whether or not the project's tracking is on: into store
(a folder or a RunStore; default the rig's project's store). Returns the run record.

### `dv.run_store(where: Rig | str | os.PathLike | RunStore | None) -> RunStore`

The run store (core/tracking/store.py RunStore) of where: a Rig (its project's store), a .dexv project file
(the store its tracking settings name, default <name>.runs beside it) or a run store folder.

### `dv.prices(kind: str | None = None, stated_only: bool = True) -> Table`

The library's cited prices: id, kind, device, amount, currency, price kind (maker_store, maker_price_list,
reseller), min_quantity, region, source URL and date read; stated_only=False lists the entries without one too
(amount None). Nothing is estimated or converted (docs/models/library.md#prices).

### `dv.price(model_id: str) -> dict | None`

The cited price block of one library entry (a copy), or None when the entry states no price.

### `dv.diff(a: Rig | Project | str | os.PathLike, b: Rig | Project | str | os.PathLike, metrics: str | Sequence[str] | None = None) -> Diff`

What changed from a to b (each a Rig, a Project or a path). metrics: metric ids (dv.metrics()) to run on both
projects and compare; their studies run in this thread.

### `dv.merge(base: Rig | Project | str | os.PathLike, ours: Rig | Project | str | os.PathLike, theirs: Rig | Project | str | os.PathLike) -> Merge`

Merge two edits (ours, theirs) of one project (base); each a Rig, a Project or a path. Places changed
differently on both sides raise dv.MergeConflict (a DexVantageError) whose .conflicts lists them in words.

### `dv.bibtex(rig: Rig | Project | str | os.PathLike | None, path: str | os.PathLike | None = None, references: str = 'checks') -> str`

BibTeX of every source the rig depends on: DexVantage, its library entries' datasheets, its robots' model
files, its datasets and the validation references (references: 'checks' those the checks cite, 'all', 'none').
path: also write it there. Returns the text.

### `dv.figures(result: Result | dict) -> list`

The publication figure specs of a study result (a dv Result or its dict), as the paper kit draws them: a list
of {'id', 'study', 'spec'}; empty when the result has no per-item list of numbers to chart.

### `dv.figure(source: Result | dict | str | os.PathLike, path: str | os.PathLike, width: str | float = 'single', palette: str = 'tol', index: int = 0, **options: object) -> dict`

Write a vector figure: source is a figure spec (dexvantage.figure/1, a dict, JSON text or a .json file), a
{'spec': ...} item of dv.figures(), or a study result (its figure number index). width: 'single' (88.9 mm),
'double' (182 mm) or millimetres; palette 'tol' (colour-blind safe, the default) or 'chart'. The format follows
the extension (.svg or .pdf). Returns {'path', 'format', 'width_mm', 'height_mm', 'series'}.

### `dv.export_runs(where: Rig | str | os.PathLike | RunStore | None, out_dir: str | os.PathLike, formats: str | Sequence[str] = ('csv', 'parquet', 'mlflow', 'wandb'), **filters: object) -> dict`

Write the runs of a run store (dv.run_store(where): a Rig, a .dexv file or a store folder) into out_dir as
runs.csv / runs_long.csv, runs.parquet, mlruns/ (MLflow's file store layout) and wandb/ (a W&B offline replay),
with a manifest (SHA-256 and provenance). filters as dv.runs (study, tag, kind, status, project, since, until).
Returns {'files', 'formats': {format: {'status', 'files', 'notes' or 'reason'}}, 'runs', 'manifest'}.

## Classes

### `dv.Rig(project: Project)`

A DexVantage project (core.project.Project) seen from Python: its robots, sensors and variants, its factors,
its studies, metrics, exports and requirements. Rig(project) wraps a Project; dv.open / dv.sample / dv.new make
one.

#### `Rig.add_variant(name: str, factors: dict | None = None, from_variant: str | None = None, allow_locked: bool = False) -> Variant`

Add a variant to this rig (edits it, as the window's "New variant from this one"): a copy of from_variant
(a name or uid; default the active one) called name, with the sensor factors given set on the copy, e.g.
rig.add_variant('Raised overhead', {'sensor:cam_high (overhead).dz': 0.05}). Its sensors keep their uids, so
host links, cables and policy cameras apply to it too; the active variant does not change. Returns the
Variant (dv.stats.compare_variants(rig, b=name) compares the two).

#### `Rig.apply_sim2real(change: dict) -> Rig`

A NEW Rig with one sim-to-real suggestion made (a result's 'apply', or a cause's 'apply'); rig is
unchanged. A locked sensor is refused (DexVantageError).

#### `Rig.check(requirements: str | os.PathLike | list | None = None, variant: str | None = None) -> Result`

The readiness scorecard: requirements is a requirements file (YAML or JSON), a list of requirement dicts,
'defaults' (DexVantage's labelled defaults) or None (the rig's own). Returns a Result whose headline is the
verdict ('ready', 'not ready', 'not evaluated').

#### `Rig.copy() -> Rig`

No docstring.

#### `Rig.export(out_dir: str, formats: str | list, options: dict | None = None) -> dict`

Write the rig in the given formats (dv.exporters() lists them) into out_dir; returns the manifest
(formats with their files, notes and status; every file's SHA-256; export_manifest.json beside them).

#### `Rig.factors`

No docstring.

#### `Rig.gap_dataset(folder: str, gaps: dict, progress: Callable[[float, str], None] | None = None, **settings: object) -> dict`

Render a synthetic LeRobot dataset with KNOWN sim-to-real gaps (brightness_dn, gain, blur_px, noise_dn,
mount, latency_s, camera: core/sim2real/inject.py) into a new or empty folder; returns its summary.

#### `Rig.metrics(ids: str | list) -> MetricTable`

The named metrics (core/metrics.py ids; dv.metrics() lists them), each study run at most once.

#### `Rig.name`

No docstring.

#### `Rig.new(name: str = 'Untitled') -> Rig`

No docstring.

#### `Rig.open(path: str) -> Rig`

No docstring.

#### `Rig.path`

No docstring.

#### `Rig.project`

The underlying core.project.Project (the same object: changing it changes the rig).

#### `Rig.robots`

No docstring.

#### `Rig.run(study: str, *, progress: Callable[[float, str], None] | None = None, **settings: object) -> Result`

Run a study (its id, e.g. 'coverage', or its batch flag, e.g. 'grasp') on a copy of the rig with
settings laid over the stored ones; the rig is unchanged. progress: fn(fraction, text). A setting name the
study does not read is refused in one sentence that lists its settings (core/study_settings.py).

#### `Rig.sample(name: str) -> Rig`

No docstring.

#### `Rig.save(path: str | None = None) -> str`

Write the .dexv file (to path, or where it was opened from; a folder or a path ending in .dexv.d: the
unpacked, Git-friendly form); returns the path.

#### `Rig.sensor_rows() -> list`

No docstring.

#### `Rig.sensors`

The active variant's sensors.

#### `Rig.sim2real(dataset: str | os.PathLike, *, progress: Callable[[float, str], None] | None = None, **settings: object) -> Result`

The sim-to-real gap of a recorded episode (core/sim2real/gap.py: the episode rendered again through the rig
and compared per camera, the causes ranked with their changes); dataset is a path (LeRobot, RLDS, ROS 2 bag).
The same as run('sim2real', dataset=path, ...).

#### `Rig.synth_episodes(folder: str, progress: Callable[[float, str], None] | None = None, **settings: object) -> dict`

Render synthetic LeRobot episodes with known faults into a new or empty folder (core/sim/episodes.py;
needs MuJoCo's offscreen renderer); returns its summary.

#### `Rig.to_frame() -> Records | pd.DataFrame`

The active variant's sensors, one row each (mount pose in the parent frame).

#### `Rig.use_variant(ident: str) -> Rig`

A new Rig with the variant named (by name or uid) active.

#### `Rig.variant`

No docstring.

#### `Rig.variants`

No docstring.

#### `Rig.with_factors(values: dict, allow_locked: bool = False) -> Rig`

A new Rig with these factors set (core/factors.py paths); this rig is unchanged.

### `dv.Result(doc: dict, study: str = '', title: str = '', project: Project | None = None)`

A study's result: the study's own JSON document (a dict: res['summary'], json.dumps(res)) plus

.study, .title        the study id and its title
.headline             {'metric', 'title', 'value', 'unit', 'better', 'status', 'bound', 'level', 'word',
                       'text'}: the study's headline figure (its metric tagged 'headline') with the status
                       word the result gives, or None when the study has no headline metric
.metrics()            every metric of this study read off this result (no re-run): a MetricTable
.to_frame(key=None, columns=None)
                      key None: the metrics, one row each; else the list (or dict) under that key, one row
                      per item, nested fields as dotted columns (columns= keeps only those): a pandas
                      DataFrame, or Records
.tables()             the keys that hold lists of rows (what to_frame(key) takes)
.save(path)           JSON with the provenance block (core/provenance.py)

#### `Result.headline`

No docstring.

#### `Result.metrics() -> MetricTable`

No docstring.

#### `Result.rows(key: str | None = None) -> list`

No docstring.

#### `Result.save(path: str) -> str`

Write the result as JSON with the provenance block; returns the path.

#### `Result.tables() -> list`

No docstring.

#### `Result.to_frame(key: str | None = None, columns: list | None = None) -> Records | pd.DataFrame`

A table of the result (the class docstring); columns: keep only these (dotted names for nested fields).

### `dv.DexVantageError(…)`

A study cannot run on this project; the message says why in plain words (shown in the UI, never a traceback).

### `dv.Diff(doc: dict, project: Project | None = None)`

What changed from project a to project b (core/projdiff.diff's document): 'a', 'b', 'identical', 'counts',
'changes' (section, op, kind, item, field, path, before, after, text) and 'metrics' (the deltas asked for).

#### `Diff.html`

A standalone HTML page of the diff.

#### `Diff.identical`

No docstring.

#### `Diff.save(path: str) -> str`

The diff as JSON with the provenance block of project a (as --diff A --diff B OUT.json writes it).

#### `Diff.text`

No docstring.

#### `Diff.to_frame(key: str = 'changes') -> Records | pd.DataFrame`

One row per change (key='metrics': one row per metric delta): a pandas DataFrame, or Records.

### `dv.Merge(res: MergeResult)`

A three-way merge: .rig (the merged Rig, not yet saved), .from_ours and .from_theirs (the places only one side
changed), .notes (what the merge noticed, such as two sensors that now share a name).

### `dv.MergeConflict(text, conflicts=())`

The two edits cannot be merged; .conflicts lists each conflicting place in words.

## Namespaces

Objects whose methods group one area: call them as `dv.<name>.<method>(…)`.

### `dv.datasets`

dv.datasets: open(path) -> Recording; formats() -> the formats DexVantage reads (plugins' too).

### `dv.publication`

dv.publication: the publication kit (core/publication.py) of a rig, headless.

    dv.publication.methods(rig, results)          the methods paragraph (TeX), every number traced
    dv.publication.tables(rig, results)           {name: TeX table} (sensors, results, scorecard, ...)
    dv.publication.kit(rig, results)              the whole kit as data, with its checks and status
    dv.publication.export(rig, 'out/', results)   main.tex, methods.tex, tables/, figures/, refs.bib, ...

results: {study id: result} or a list of results (rig.run(...) gives them); without results every study but the
long meta-studies runs first, as the report does (pass studies=[...] to choose). Other keyword options are the
kit's settings: sections, siunitx, widths, pdf_figures, bibliography, title, validation, figure_specs. The PDF
figures (export only) use Qt's PDF writer; nothing else imports Qt.

#### `dv.publication.export(rig: Rig | Project, out_dir: str, results: dict | list | None = None, **options: object) -> dict`

No docstring.

### `dv.cells`

dv.cells: compare(*cells, reference=0, metrics=None, tolerance_draws=0, seed=1, pooling='auto',
variants=False, progress=None) -> CellComparison.

A cell is a Rig (dv.open, dv.sample), a core Project, a path to a .dexv file or folder, or 'sample:<name>'; the
first is the reference unless reference= names another (by number). metrics: metric ids, 'all', or None (the
quick figures, core/cells.DEFAULT_METRICS); tolerance_draws ≥ 2 runs the tolerance Monte Carlo on every cell to say
which differences exceed the build spread; pooling: 'auto' (a recorded dataset where a cell has one, else its
plan), 'plan' or 'recorded'; variants=True adds the first cell's other variants as cells.

```pycon
>>> import dexvantage as dv
>>> res = dv.cells.compare(dv.sample('so100'), 'sample:so100', metrics=['rig.camera_count'])
>>> res.headline['value'], res['pooling']['text']
(0.0, 'Every cell pools as is.')
```

#### `dv.cells.compare(*cells: Rig | Project | str | os.PathLike, reference: int = 0, metrics: list | None = None, tolerance_draws: int = 0, seed: int = 1, pooling: str = 'auto', variants: bool = False, progress: Callable[[float, str], None] | None = None) -> CellComparison`

### `dv.stats`

dv.stats: tests, effect sizes, corrections and power analysis (core/stats.py, every function of it is here:
dv.stats.wilson, .clopper_pearson, .bootstrap_ci, .permutation_test, .welch_t, .mann_whitney,
.wilcoxon_signed_rank, .cohens_d, .cliffs_delta, .risk_difference, .odds_ratio, .fisher_exact, .adjust,
.power_two_proportions, .power_t, .n_two_proportions, .n_t, .episodes_needed, .demonstrations_needed, ...) and the
app's comparisons:

    compare_rates(rows, compare='reference', test='fisher', ...)     -> Result (the 'stats' study)
    compare_samples(a, b, paired=False, title='', unit='', better='higher', ...) -> Result
    compare_variants(rig, a=None, b=None, metrics=None, n=32, seed=0, ...)       -> Result (tolerance draws,
                                                                                     paired by seed)
    compare_experiment(rig, factor, levels=None, result=None, ...)              -> Result
    compare_runs(rig, a, b, folder=None, metrics=None, ...)                     -> Result (tracker runs)
    run(spec, rig=None)                                                         -> Result (a spec dict or file)

```pycon
>>> import dexvantage as dv
>>> dv.stats.episodes_needed(0.5, 0.8)['n_per_group']
44
>>> r = dv.stats.compare_rates([('ACT', 14, 20), ('Diffusion', 19, 20)])
>>> r.headline['word'], round(r['comparisons'][0]['p'], 4)
('no clear difference', 0.0915)
```

#### `dv.stats.compare_experiment(rig: Rig | Project, factor: str, levels: list | None = None, result: Result | dict | str | os.PathLike | None = None, responses: list | None = None, progress: Callable[[float, str], None] | None = None, **settings: object) -> Result`

An experiment's runs split by factor's two levels (result: an experiment Result, its dict or a file;
default the experiment saved in rig, run).

#### `dv.stats.compare_rates(rows: list, compare: str = 'reference', test: str = 'fisher', power: dict | None = None, **settings: object) -> Result`

rows: [(condition, successes, trials)] or [{'condition', 'successes', 'trials'}].

#### `dv.stats.compare_runs(rig: Rig | Project, a: str | list | dict, b: str | list | dict, folder: str | None = None, metrics: list | None = None, **settings: object) -> Result`

Tracker runs: a and b each a run id, a list of ids or {'tag': t}.

#### `dv.stats.compare_samples(a: Sequence[float], b: Sequence[float], paired: bool = False, title: str = 'Value', unit: str = '', better: str = 'higher', names: tuple | list = ('A', 'B'), **settings: object) -> Result`

No docstring.

#### `dv.stats.compare_variants(rig: Rig | Project, a: str | None = None, b: str | None = None, metrics: list | None = None, n: int = 32, seed: int = 0, scale: float = 1.0, distribution: str = 'uniform', progress: Callable[[float, str], None] | None = None, **settings: object) -> Result`

Two variants of rig over the tolerance Monte Carlo with one seed (the draws paired by seed).

#### `dv.stats.run(spec: dict | str | os.PathLike, rig: Rig | Project | None = None, progress: Callable[[float, str], None] | None = None) -> Result`

A statistics spec (a dict, JSON text or a spec file: schema dexvantage.stats/1) on rig (None: success
counts, samples and the power calculator need no project).

### `dv.robot_io`

dv.robot_io: robot files in and out, headless.

dv.robot_io.convert_usd('arm.usda')          # {'name', 'mjcf', 'meshes', 'notes', 'record'}: a UsdPhysics
                                             # articulation as MJCF (core/robot/usd_import.py; needs usd-core)
robot = dv.robot_io.add_robot(rig, 'arm.usda')   # import a URDF, MJCF or USD robot into rig (edits rig)
dv.robot_io.write_usd(rig, "arm.usda")       # a robot as a UsdPhysics articulation (core/robot/usd_writer)
dv.robot_io.openvla_encoding(rig)            # the OXE state / action encodings the OpenVLA export writes

#### `dv.robot_io.add_robot(rig: Rig, path: str | os.PathLike, name: str | None = None) -> Robot`

Import the robot file at path (URDF, MJCF or USD) into rig's project (the first robot is primary); the
Robot added. Edits rig.

#### `dv.robot_io.convert_usd(path: str | os.PathLike) -> dict`

No docstring.

#### `dv.robot_io.openvla_encoding(rig: Rig, action_space: str | None = None) -> dict`

No docstring.

#### `dv.robot_io.write_usd(rig: Rig, path: str | os.PathLike, robot: str | None = None) -> dict`

Write rig's robot (a name or uid; default the primary) as a UsdPhysics articulation at path.

## The plugin SDK (`dexvantage.plugin_sdk`)

Plugins: third-party packages that add studies, metrics, exporters, dataset readers, library folders, UI pages and
the validation checks of their models to DexVantage without editing it.

A plugin is an installed Python distribution that declares an entry point in the group ``dexvantage.plugins``:

    # the plugin's pyproject.toml
    [project.entry-points."dexvantage.plugins"]
    my_plugin = "my_plugin:register"

    # my_plugin/__init__.py
    def register(api):                     # api: a PluginAPI, one per plugin
        api.study('my_study', 'My study', batch='my-study')(my_study_fn)
        api.metric('my.figure', 'My figure', 'mm', 'lower', study='my_study')(lambda doc: doc['summary']['mm'])
        api.exporter('my_format', 'My format')(my_export_fn)
        api.dataset_reader('my_format', sniff=my_sniff)(my_open_fn)
        api.library_folder(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'library'))
        api.check('my.vs_closed_form', 'My study against a closed form', 'mm error', 'the closed form',
                  0.01, 'mm', references={'me2026': 'A. Author, "Title", URL (read 2026-11-07).'})(my_check_fn)
                                           # a validation check of the plugin's model (plugin.my_plugin), run by
                                           # --validate and Help ▸ Validate the models with the built-in checks
        api.page('my_page', 'My study', 'my_plugin.page:MyPage', menu='Analysis')   # the class is imported only
                                                                                     # when the window is built

The entry point may name a function or a module (its ``register`` is called). DexVantage loads plugins once at start-up
(app.py, before the batch flags are built, so a plugin study gets its ``--flag`` too), and the Python API loads them on
first use (dexvantage.api). Help ▸ Plugins lists every plugin found: its name, version, what it added and, for a plugin
that failed, why, in a plain sentence. A plugin that fails is rolled back (what it added before the failure is removed)
and the app carries on; its traceback goes to the log (stderr), never to the UI.

``--no-plugins`` (or the environment variable DEXVANTAGE_NO_PLUGINS=1) finds the installed plugins without loading
them: they are listed as "off".

Rules a plugin follows (checked where they can be): ids are new (a plugin cannot replace a built-in study, metric,
exporter or dataset format: the duplicate is skipped and said so); study ids are lower-case words joined by
underscores (no dots: factor paths and settings use the dot); a page class is given as "module:Class" so headless use
never imports Qt; a plugin's figures follow docs/DEVELOPING.md like DexVantage's own (cited or None). A plugin may set
``REQUIRES_API = n`` in its module; one that needs a newer plugin API than API_VERSION is refused with a sentence.

API
    load(enabled=True, entry_points=None, paths=None) -> [PluginRecord]   once; again with reload=True
    loaded() -> [PluginRecord]                         what the last load found (for Help ▸ Plugins and dv.plugins())
    discover(paths=None) -> [EntryPoint]               the installed entry points of the group (paths: search there)
    unload(name)                                       remove what a plugin added (tests; a plugin turned off)
    origin(kind, id) -> plugin name | None             which plugin added a study / metric / exporter / reader / page /
                                                       check
    summary_text(record) -> str                        "2 studies (a, b), 1 metric (c)": what it added, in words

Known limits: a plugin runs in the same process with the same rights as DexVantage (there is no sandbox: install only
plugins you trust); unloading removes what a plugin registered, not modules it imported or state it changed in other
ways; UI pages are added when the window is built, so a plugin loaded later (from the Python API in a running window)
adds its page only after a restart; a page whose id equals a built-in page's id is replaced by the built-in one (the
plugin's record says so: page_replaced).

### `plugin_sdk.PluginAPI(record: PluginRecord)`

What a plugin's register(api) receives: one per plugin, recording what it adds (shown in Help ▸ Plugins and
removed again when the plugin fails or is unloaded).

#### `PluginAPI.Outcome`

What a validation check returns (validation/suite.py Outcome: error, detail, figure, rows, ...).

#### `PluginAPI.StudyError`

No docstring.

#### `PluginAPI.check(cid: str, title: str, quantity: str, reference: str, tolerance: float, unit: str, references: dict | None = None, refs: Iterable[str] | None = None, cost: str = 'cheap', tolerance_quick: float | None = None, model_title: str = '') -> Callable[[Callable], Callable]`

Decorator: register fn(ctx) -> api.Outcome as a validation check (validation/suite.py @check) of this
plugin's model, 'plugin.<plugin name>' (model_title: its title in the report, default "<name> (plugin)"), so
--validate, the self-test's cheap run and Help ▸ Validate the models run it with DexVantage's own checks.
reference: the independent reference in words; tolerance: the error the check accepts (say why in the
reference or the plugin's docs, as docs/DEVELOPING.md asks); references: {key: the full citation with its URL
and the date read}, added to the report's reference list (refs: the keys this check cites, default all of
references; a key DexVantage already has may be cited by name).

#### `PluginAPI.dataset_reader(fmt: str, sniff: Callable[[str], bool], title: str = '') -> Callable[[Callable], Callable]`

Decorator: register open(path) -> core.datasets.Dataset for the format fmt; sniff(path) -> bool says
whether a path is in it. title: the format's name in words ('' = fmt).

#### `PluginAPI.dv`

The Python API (dexvantage.api): dv.sample, Rig, Result, ...

#### `PluginAPI.exporter(fid: str, title: str, needs_robot: bool = False, description: str = '') -> Callable[[Callable], Callable]`

Decorator: register fn(project, out_dir, options, ctx) -> {'files', 'notes'} (core.exporters.exporter).

#### `PluginAPI.jobs`

No docstring.

#### `PluginAPI.library_folder(path: str) -> None`

Read library entries (one JSON per device, the library schema) from this folder too; read-only, like the
built-in library. Entries whose id is already taken are skipped (Library problems say so).

#### `PluginAPI.metric(mid: str, title: str, unit: str, better: str, study: str, note: str = '', tags: Iterable[str] = ()) -> Callable[[Callable], Callable]`

Decorator: register extract(doc) -> float | None as a metric (core.metrics.metric).

#### `PluginAPI.page(pid: str, title: str, cls: type | str, menu: str = 'Analysis', icon: str | None = None, action_id: str | None = None, shortcut: str | None = None, workspace: str | None = None, order: int = 200) -> type | str`

A UI page (ui/pages registry). cls: a StudyPage subclass or "module:Class" (imported when the window is
built: headless use of the plugin never imports Qt).

#### `PluginAPI.study(sid: str, title: str, quick: bool = False, batch: str = '', needs_robot: bool = False) -> Callable[[Callable], Callable]`

Decorator: register fn(project, ctx) -> dict as a study (core.jobs.study). batch: its batch flag without
dashes ('' for none).

### `plugin_sdk.PluginError(…)`

A plugin asked for something DexVantage cannot give it; the message says what, in plain words.

### `plugin_sdk.discover(paths: Iterable[str | os.PathLike] | None = None) -> list`

The entry points of the group: installed ones, or those of the distributions found on paths (folders, as
importlib.metadata searches them: a pip --target folder, a site-packages).

### `plugin_sdk.load(enabled: bool | None = None, entry_points: Iterable[EntryPoint] | None = None, paths: Iterable[str | os.PathLike] | None = None, reload: bool = False) -> list`

Find and load the plugins once (again with reload=True, which unloads the previous ones first). enabled=None
follows DEXVANTAGE_NO_PLUGINS; False finds them without loading (status 'off'). entry_points: load these
instead of the installed ones (tests); paths: find them on these folders instead of sys.path.

### `plugin_sdk.loaded() -> list`

No docstring.

### `plugin_sdk.enabled() -> bool`

False when this session was started with --no-plugins (or DEXVANTAGE_NO_PLUGINS).

### `plugin_sdk.unload(name: str) -> None`

Remove everything the named plugin added (studies, metrics, exporters, readers, library folders, pages, checks
with their model and references).

### `plugin_sdk.report_lines() -> list`

One plain line per plugin, for the terminal (--list-plugins) and the self-test.
